title: Integral scalar global Hom on a fixed K-injective target
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l and X a scheme, with completed coefficient sheaf O_X and R=O_E lifted to its section universe. For any K-injective complex I of O_X-module sheaves, the functor on the opposite category of all complexes P given by RΓ_X(RHom(QP,QI)) is naturally isomorphic in D(R) to QΓ_R(Hom(P,I)). Here Γ_R is linear Hom from the unit restricted along the actual constant-to-completion map R→Γ(O_X), and RΓ_X is derived evaluation at the final pro-etale object with the same scalar action. No inverse limit or tower occurs in this assertion.

source.place: section-global-RHom (Tag 0B6E), section on internal Hom (Tags 0A95, 0A96), lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (Tag 0941); current blueprint prop-coef-integral-dualizing, second proof paragraph.

proof.text: Evaluate a unit-module morphism at 1 on the final pro-etale object. Its inverse extends a terminal section by restriction and applies unitHomEquiv.symm. Naturality and the sectionwise module action show this is an integral-linear natural isomorphism from the specified linear unit-Hom sections to integralDualizingSections.
Restrict the proved natural internal-Hom representative comparison to the fixed K-injective I. This gives RHom(Q(-),QI) naturally isomorphic to Q Hom(-,I) before applying derived sections.

Whisker the canonical derived-sections unit by Hom(-,I). For any source L choose a K-flat resolution P to L; Hom(P,I) is K-injective, so the unit is invertible there. Precomposition is a quasi-isomorphism on sheaf Hom, and on sections at the final object after forgetting integral scalars. The faithful exact module-to-abelian-group functor reflects this latter quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the unit therefore makes its component at Hom(L,I) invertible. Compose its inverse with the internal-Hom comparison and the termwise scalar-sections isomorphism.
